meta: Online easy-job, high-pay scams: the signs to spot before you lose money.

muc.title: An offer too good to be true
muc.text: An ad for a work-from-home job, a few hours a day with high pay, is often the first step of a scam.

muc.title: Three common signs
muc.text: The signs: the work is too easy and the pay too high, hiring happens in chat groups, and you must pay a fee or deposit first.

muc.title: Small rewards, then they keep the big money
muc.text: Scammers pay small rewards a few times so you trust them, then make you deposit large sums for tasks and keep it all.

muc.title: Call your bank and the police
muc.text: If you've sent money, call your bank right away, report it to the police, and don't send more to get it back.

muc.title: Check one job ad
muc.text: Paste an online job ad into a chatbot, an AI chat assistant, and ask it to point out what's suspicious.
